title: Evaluating the impact of adversarial traffic patterns on vanet communication using veins simulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.14583v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) are a key component of intelligent transportation systems, enabling real-time communication between vehicles. However, their open and dynamic nature makes them highly vulnerable to adversarial behaviors that can disrupt communication reliability. This paper investigates the impact of adversarial traffic patterns on VANET performance using the Veins simulation framework integrated with OMNeT++ and SUMO. We design and evaluate multiple adversarial scenarios, including message flooding, false information dissemination, and coordinated congestion attacks, under varying traffic densities and mobility conditions. The study measures key performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), end-to-end delay, and network throughput. translated_title: 评估对抗性交通模式对基于Veins仿真的VANET通信的影响
translated_abstract: 车载自组织网络（VANET）是智能交通系统的关键组成部分，能够实现车辆间的实时通信。然而，其开放性和动态性使其极易受到对抗性行为的影响，这些行为可能破坏通信可靠性。本文利用集成OMNeT++和SUMO的Veins仿真框架，研究了对抗性交通模式对VANET性能的影响。我们设计并评估了多种对抗性场景，包括消息洪泛、虚假信息传播和协调拥塞攻击，并在不同交通密度和移动条件下进行测试。研究测量了数据包投递率（PDR）、端到端延迟和网络吞吐量等关键性能指标。实验结果表明，对抗性交通可使PDR降低高达96.55%，其中低密度下的消息洪泛导致吞吐量降低27.89%，并显著影响网络性能。
tldr: 本文通过Veins仿真系统研究了对抗性交通模式（如消息洪泛、虚假信息和拥塞攻击）对VANET通信性能的严重影响，发现PDR可降低96.55%，揭示了此类攻击对网络可靠性的显著破坏力。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates the impact of adversarial traffic patterns (e.g., message flooding, false information, and congestion attacks) on VANET communication using Veins simulation, showing PDR degradation up to 96.55% and significant throughput loss, highlighting their severe threat to network reliability.
